playbook.strategy: Full-quota cooperation in this commons game produces a perfectly stable equilibrium where all boats harvest 3 each round, stock returns to 27 after each regrowth, and all players tie at identical scores. This episode confirms that alignment is rewarded over defection and that rivals will reciprocate a cooperation signal immediately. On the first move of any new episode, signal cooperation by taking your full quota of 3; if all rivals match this signal in the first round, lock into full-quota strategy for all remaining rounds—the pattern will likely sustain and produce a tied outcome at 12 points (or proportionally higher if more rounds are available). Do not underharvest to test rivals or to appear cautious; that only leaves points on the table and may break the equilibrium if rivals interpret it as a defection signal. Do not overharvest or dump unless you observe a rival clearly defecting (taking significantly less than 2 or more than 3). If the stock ever drops below 27 mid-round, immediately check whether rivals' total catch is less than 9; if so, investigate whether someone is deliberately constraining catch to signal conservation or if a rule assumption has changed. The final round offers no endgame advantage to defecting—harvest normally and expect rivals to do the same. Always calculate the equilibrium early: if stock cap and regrowth rate allow all boats to take full quota without depleting, commit to that pattern and expect rivals to follow. Dumping is almost never profitable (−1 point per fish) unless you can prove it denies an opponent 2+ points in aggregate, which is rare in a symmetric game; reserve it for last-resort punishment or desperation. Ties under full cooperation are acceptable outcomes and strongly preferable to costly defection races. The quota of 3 has never been exceeded in practice; treat it as a hard constraint until evidence proves otherwise.
